findings.claim: The serializer method `include_website_name` lacks the trailing `?` that ActiveModel::Serializer requires for `include_<attr>?` predicates. As a result it is never called and `website_name` is always serialized, as null when there is no website.

verifier.reason: In app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:153-155, the patch defines `def include_website_name` without a trailing `?`, whereas ActiveModel::Serializer (v0.8.3) requires `include_<attr>?` predicates (as used throughout UserSerializer). Because `include_website_name?` is undefined, the method is never invoked and `:website_name` (app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:43) is always serialized, returning `nil` (JSON `null`) via `return if website_host.nil?` at app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:140 when no website is set.

findings.claim: UserSerializer's `website_name` does not honor `Guardian#restrict_user_fields?` and is not in `untrusted_attributes`, unlike `website`. This exposes the website host/path of TL0 users to anonymous viewers.

verifier.reason: In app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:43,105-111,137-155, `:website_name` is serialized as an attribute but omitted from `untrusted_attributes` (unlike `:website`), and neither `website_name` nor `include_website_name` checks `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`. As a result, TL0 users' website host/path is exposed to anonymous viewers in both the API payload and user profile template, whereas previously it was derived client-side from the restricted `model.website`.
